title: Align the pity cohort histogram's bars and markers on one x domain
body:
## Summary
PityCohortChart places bars over nBins*binW kills but percentile markers and axis ticks over max kills, so they drift apart when max is not a multiple of binW.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/pity/PityCohortChart.tsx sets binW=ceil(max/40), nBins=ceil(max/binW); bars at LEFT+i*bw with bw=(RIGHT-LEFT)/nBins cover nBins*binW kills, while x(kill)=LEFT+kill/max*(RIGHT-LEFT) positions P50/P95/P99 and the 0/50%/100% ticks. For max=97 the bars span 99 kills: a marker lands up to 2% of the width away from the bar holding its kill. Fixed = one domain (nBins*binW) for bars, markers and ticks.

## Flow
- cohort with max kill 97 -> binW 3, nBins 33
- P95 marker x uses /97, its bin's bar uses /99
- marker sits left of the bar it labels

## Expected impact
Designers reading the percentile line against the histogram see it over the right bar; nothing else reads these coordinates.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - markers sit on the bar holding their kill
Before: walked: max=97 -> 2.0% offset; max=2000 and max=20 -> 0%
After: 0% for any max
Method: simulation - three maxes walked (97, 2000, 20); an S test asserting marker x inside its bin's rect for max=97 is the instrument, not built this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/pity/PityCohortChart.tsx (view memo binW/nBins; x(); bar rect x)
instrument: vitest: stub usePityCohort with kills max 97; assert x(P95) lies inside the rect of bin floor((P95-1)/binW)

title: Share one high-gear-gap threshold between smart-loot lift and its badge
body:
## Summary
SmartLoot's effectiveness figure counts slots with gearScoreGap >= 10 but badges slots with gap > 10.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/simulation/lootSimEngine.ts smartLootLift(minGap = 10) filters gearScoreGap >= minGap; src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/economy/SmartLoot.tsx shows the Gap badge only when gearScoreGap > 10. Two copies of one rule with different comparators; no shipped slot has gap exactly 10 (SMART_LOOT_DATA gaps 15,3,12,8,20,2,5,1), so it is latent. Fixed = export one SMART_LOOT_HIGH_GAP predicate used by both.

## Flow
- tune a slot to gearScoreGap 10
- lift counts it as high-gap
- no badge marks it

## Expected impact
The 'N% more drops to high-gap slots' figure and the badged slots agree.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one predicate for 'high-gap slot'
Before: 2 predicates (>= vs >); 0 visible mismatches on shipped data
After: 1 predicate
Method: simulation - latent on shipped data; a vi.mock of SMART_LOOT_DATA with a gap-10 slot is the instrument
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest with vi.mock of _shared/data-binding adding a gap-10 slot: badge count must equal smartLootLift().slots

title: Derive the drop treemap's probabilities from RARITY_TIERS instead of a copy
body:
## Summary
TREEMAP_DATA hand-copies the rarity weights (50/25/15/8/2) that RARITY_TIERS already owns.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/_shared/data.ts:89-95 lists probability per tier by hand; src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/_shared/data.ts:40-46 RARITY_TIERS holds the same weights. Retuning a tier weight leaves the treemap (and its new keyboard names) on the old value. Fixed = probability = weight / TOTAL_WEIGHT * 100 from RARITY_TIERS, affixes kept. The list lives in _shared (loot-affix-core), out of this round's paths.

## Flow
- edit RARITY_TIERS Legendary weight 2 -> 4
- Monte Carlo and Drop Simulator follow
- treemap still says Legendary 2%

## Expected impact
Treemap tracks the rarity table; a test pins equality.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one authority for tier probability
Before: 2 hand-maintained copies
After: 1
Method: probe - read both lists: equal today, coupled by hand only
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: for each RARITY_TIERS t, treemap probability === t.weight/TOTAL_WEIGHT*100, seeded by mutating a weight

title: Label the Drops-per-Hour panel's player profile and level scaling
body:
## Summary
DropsPerHour derives from the casual profile (120 kills/h) without saying so, and scales gold and Time-to-Legendary by an unexplained 1+0.04*(level-1).

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/simulation/DropsPerHour.tsx hard-codes deriveEconomy(..., 'casual') while the Economy tab offers Casual/Hardcore; levelMultiplier (0.04/level) multiplies items AND gold and divides Time to Legendary, though its aria-valuetext calls it a drop-rate multiplier. The level scale is not in lootSimEngine, so a second scaling bypasses the engine. Fixed = profile shown or selectable via profileScale, level scale named in the engine with an explicit target.

## Flow
- open Drops per Hour
- gauge reads Items/Hour with no profile
- Economy tab Hardcore shows a different figure for the same roster

## Expected impact
Designers can tell which player the gauge describes; risk is copy/layout only.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the gauge states its profile and scaling
Before: 0 of 2 assumptions labelled
After: 2 of 2
Method: simulation - read the component; whether level should scale gold is a design call
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
instrument: none - needs the owner to decide whether level scales gold

title: Derive the drop-source breakdown and gauge targets from the tuned roster
body:
## Summary
DropsPerHour's Drop Source Breakdown (40/30/20/10) and the gauges' targets are fixed literals beside derived current values.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/_shared/data.ts:109-117 DROPS_PER_HOUR_GAUGE/GOLD_PER_HOUR_GAUGE targets and DROP_SOURCE_BREAKDOWN are constants; src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/simulation/DropsPerHour.tsx paints them next to deriveEconomy output. The recorded registry deviation (game-economy-tuning, EconomySummaryGrid fixed strings) was cured for the grid by a28dbc93; the breakdown is the remaining fixed figure on the tab. Fixed = breakdown from per-archetype dropChance share grouped by tier; targets from a named balance band. Touches _shared (out of scope).

## Flow
- tune every Minion dropChance to 0
- breakdown still shows Grunt 40%

## Expected impact
The breakdown answers 'where do my drops come from' for the tuned roster.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every figure on the tab derived from the roster
Before: 1 of 3 figure groups derived (current values); breakdown + targets static
After: 3 of 3
Method: probe - read the render path: breakdown never reads the store
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: dispatch setField dropChance 0 on every Minion; breakdown's minion share must read 0%

title: Give the pity threshold one meaning across the timer and the drought calculator
body:
## Summary
One store value, pityThreshold, means 'drops until a guaranteed Rare+' in PityTimerSection but 'kills until a guaranteed <selected rarity>' in DroughtCalculator.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/pity/PityTimerSection.tsx doPityDrop counts DROPS and forces any of Rare/Epic/Legendary (25% of drops); its slider aria-label says 'drops before a Rare+ is guaranteed'. src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/pity/DroughtCalculator.tsx applies the same threshold per KILL to the single chosen rarity (Legendary 2%), and PityCohortChart simulates that. Fixed = one model (counter unit + guaranteed tier set) carried by the store and read by both, or two named thresholds.

## Flow
- set pity to 20
- timer: Rare+ guaranteed by drop 20
- drought: Legendary guaranteed by kill 20 - a different promise

## Expected impact
Designers tuning pity see one promise; the UE pity spec gets one number with one meaning. Changes what the drought figures mean.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one pity promise
Before: 2 meanings for 1 value
After: 1
Method: simulation - read both models; which one ships is a design decision
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
instrument: none - owner picks the shipped pity model

title: Map the _orphan affix panels to the context that consumes them
body:
## Summary
Four files under sub_loot/_orphan are mapped to loot-simulation but are imported only by affix-workbench/index.tsx.

## Description
Consumer grep: AffixExportPanel, ArchetypeSuggestionGrid, PowerBudgetRadar, SynergyDetector each have exactly one product consumer, src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/affix-workbench/index.tsx (plus src/__tests__/components/core-engine/affix-crafting-kernel.test.ts). None is orphaned and none is loot simulation; context-map.json lists them under loot-simulation, so a loot-affix-workbench sweep never sees them. Fixed = move to affix-workbench/ and re-map, or re-map in place.

## Flow
- sweep loot-affix-workbench
- its own panels under _orphan are outside its paths

## Expected impact
Context ownership matches imports; a move touches imports in one file.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - files mapped to the context that imports them
Before: 4 of 4 mis-mapped
After: 0
Method: probe - consumer grep across src
Result: better
Gate: architecture

title: Let the Monte Carlo panel replay the seed it displays
body:
## Summary
MonteCarloSim prints 'seed N' and the engine promises every roll is reproducible from a seed, but the UI offers no way to enter one.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/simulation/MonteCarloSim.tsx runMonteCarlo seeds from Date.now() and the Distribution header shows the seed; src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/simulation/lootSimEngine.ts header states reproducibility as the design. A designer who sees an outlier run cannot re-run it. Fixed = a seed field (defaulting to the last run) feeding runMonteCarlo.

## Flow
- run 1,000
- note the seed of an odd Legendary max
- no control re-runs that seed

## Expected impact
Outlier runs become shareable and reproducible.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a displayed seed can be replayed
Before: 0 replay paths
After: 1
Method: simulation - read the component; the engine already supports seeded runs
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: enter seed S, run 1,000 twice, assert identical stats tables

title: Caption Drop Simulator results with the enemy they were rolled for
body:
## Summary
After a roll, picking another enemy re-labels the header and banner while the counts on screen still belong to the previous enemy.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_loot/simulation/DropSimulator.tsx header button and banner read the live selectedBinding; the stored roll (fixed this round to keep its own binding for deviations, 6c1311d4) carries no name. Fixed = store archetypeName with the run and caption results 'Rolled for <name>'.

## Flow
- roll 1000 for Melee Grunt
- pick Sith Assassin without rolling
- banner says Sith Assassin over Grunt counts

## Expected impact
Results are never captioned with an enemy they were not computed for.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - result caption matches its inputs
Before: 1 mislabelled caption path
After: 0
Method: simulation - walked three selection orders
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest (mocked ScalableSelector): roll, pick another enemy, assert the results caption still names the rolled enemy
